rounds.text: Somany Ceramics Ltd is exhibiting a powerful operational inflection that the market is failing to price in, evidenced by a staggering 85% surge in trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth [E21] and a 386% year-on-year net profit explosion [E66]. Quarterly operating margins have expanded by 4 percentage points to 12% in June 2026, breaking a previously inconsistent trend and establishing four consecutive quarters of margin improvement [E31, E33, E32]. This earnings velocity is supported by exceptional financial health, demonstrated by a stellar cash conversion ratio of 3.34x and robust free cash flow of Rs 197 crore for March 2026 [E34, E36]. Furthermore, the company is aggressively expanding its footprint with a major new manufacturing plant in the South adding over 9 million square meters of capacity to unlock roughly INR 350 crores in potential revenue [E82, E84], all while funding 65% to 70% of its upcoming capex through internal accruals [E93]. Conceded: the DCF model indicates an overvaluation of 54.8% and institutional money flow has dropped by 1.88 percentage points [E46, E44]. Nevertheless, the company's relative-strength rating sits at a maximum of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51], proving that operational execution is currently overshadowing backward-looking valuation metrics.

Somany Ceramics Ltd trades at a rich valuation that is fundamentally disconnected from its historical track record, carrying a price-to-book ratio of 2.74x [E2] and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 362 against a market price of Rs 561, resulting in a severe -54.8% margin of safety [E45, E46]. This premium price tag sits atop stagnant long-term fundamentals, highlighted by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 5% [E14] and a 10-year compounded profit growth of a meager 2% [E18], which has translated into a 10-year compounded share price growth of -2% [E22]. Institutional confidence is actively eroding, evidenced by domestic institutions slashing their holdings from 23.26% in Dec 2023 to 16.04% in Sep 2026 [E43] and driving a negative money flow signal of -1.88 percentage points [E44]. Furthermore, the business faces acute external headwinds, including extreme volatility in natural gas prices with monthly increases [E94], blended gas prices sitting as high as mid-70s in the South and Morbi [E87], and exports from Morbi plunging by 50% to 60% from their peak due to geopolitical reasons [E79]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong recent operational cash flow generation with ₹197 crores in free cash flow [E36] and a notable jump in quarterly operating margin by 4 percentage points [E31].

Conceded: [E45] and [E46] show a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 362 against a market price of Rs 561, but static backward-looking models fail to capture the explosive inflection in profitability highlighted by an 85% trailing-twelve-month profit growth [E21] and a 386% year-over-year net profit surge [E66]. The bear points to a 10-year sales CAGR of 5% [E14] and profit CAGR of 2% [E18], yet ignores that recent performance is accelerating sharply, evidenced by a 9% TTM sales growth [E17] and a quarterly operating margin jumping 4 percentage points to 12% [E31]. Conceded: [E43] shows domestic institutions reducing holdings from 23.26% to 16.04%, but foreign institutional investors are moving in the opposite direction, increasing their stake from 1.43% to 2.88% [E42]. The bear's concern over natural gas price volatility [E94] is neutralized by management's proven pricing power and operational efficiency, having successfully passed on all gas price increases [E86] and driven free cash flow to a robust Rs 197 crores [E36].

Conceded: TTM profit growth reached 85% [E21] and net profit surged 386% year-over-year [E66]. However, the bull's reliance on these short-term spikes ignores a dismal structural track record of a 10-year profit CAGR of just 2% [E18] and a 10-year share price return of -2% [E22]. While the bull dismisses the discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 362 against a market price of Rs 561 [E45, E46], a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current price already bakes in an aggressive 10.0% earnings growth rate [E47]. The bull cites foreign institutional accumulation [E42], but downplays a severe domestic institutional exodus with holdings plunging from 23.26% to 16.04% [E43], resulting in an overall negative money flow signal [E44]. Finally, the bull claims management's pricing power neutralizes gas price volatility [E94], yet the record confirms that gas prices continue to exhibit extreme volatility with monthly increases [E94] while borrowings have risen to Rs 374 Cr [E39].

Conceded: the 10-year profit CAGR is 2% [E18] and the 10-year share price return is -2% [E22]. However, anchoring on decade-long history ignores the current operational turning point where TTM profit growth reached 85% [E21] and quarterly operating margins expanded by 4 percentage points year-over-year [E31]. Conceded: domestic institutional holdings declined from 23.26% to 16.04% [E43], but foreign institutions increased their stake to 2.88% [E42] while promoters also grew their holdings to 55.19% [E41]. Conceded: the DCF model calculates an intrinsic value of Rs 362 [E45], but this backward-looking valuation completely discounts the stellar cash conversion of 3.34x and robust free cash flow of Rs 197 Cr generated in Mar 2026 [E34, E36]. Finally, the bear's concern over rising borrowings to Rs 374 Cr [E39] is fully offset by moderate leverage at a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.44x [E37] and proven pricing power that successfully passed on 16% to 18% gas price increases [E86].

Conceded: TTM profit growth reached 85% [E21]. However, this short-term surge sits against a decade-long backdrop of 2% profit growth [E18] and negative 2% long-term share price returns [E22], making a single trailing period an unreliable indicator of baseline earning power. Conceded: promoters and foreign institutions slightly increased their stakes [E41, E42], but domestic institutions pulled out heavily by 7.22 percentage points [E43], driving an overall negative institutional money flow of 1.88 percentage points [E44]. Conceded: the company generated Rs 197 Cr in free cash flow [E36], but this cash generation is being aggressively redeployed into a heavy upcoming capex outlay of approximately Rs 275 crores through the end of FY27 [E92]. Finally, while management claims pricing power on gas price increases [E86], total borrowings still crept up to Rs 374 Cr [E39], operating margins remain inconsistent over a three-year horizon [E32], and the underlying valuation demands a steep 10.0% earnings growth rate against a historical 4.0% base case [E47].

evidence.quote: And we maintain that the EBITDA margins delivered in this quarter would be maintained, and we are trying to better our EBITDA margins, which we have delivered in last quarter and on this quarter.

evidence.fact: The company expects mid-single-digit volume growth for the year.
evidence.quote: Mid-single digits.

evidence.fact: Management targets to achieve 12% and more in EBITDA margins.
evidence.quote: Yes, absolutely. That's the target that we achieve 12% and more.

evidence.fact: Export from Morbi is down by 50% to 60% from the peak due to geopolitical reasons.
evidence.quote: The only negative in the quarter has been from a Morbi perspective is exports has been down due to geopolitical reasons, the export is down a good 50%, 60% from the peak.

evidence.fact: Management remains optimistic about industry growth prospects supported by sustained demand from housing, infrastructure, and renovation segments.
evidence.quote: Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the industry’s growth prospects, supported by sustained demand from housing, infrastructure, and renovation segments.

evidence.fact: Domestic demand saw a gradual improvement during January and February.
evidence.quote: as far as the quarter is concerned, the domestic demand saw a gradual improvement during January and Feb on account of increased domestic demand reducing the pressure on -- from reducing the pressure from exports.

evidence.fact: The company announced setting up a 9-plus million square meter plant in the South with an outlay of approximately INR220 crores.
evidence.quote: Because of that, we have announced setting up a 9 million square meter plant -- 9-plus million square meter plant in the South, which would be up and ready by in the next 12 to 15 months. This would give us a potential revenue of about INR350 crores.

evidence.fact: The company is adding capacity by about 4 million to 5 million in existing lines across Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, and the South.
evidence.quote: Other than that, we are taking many more steps, which are all work in progress to augment further capacity by about 4 million to 5 million in our existing lines in Bahadurgarh in -- which is in Haryana and in Gujarat and in Morbi and also in the South.

evidence.fact: The Company announced a new manufacturing facility to cater to the growing Southern market with an annual capacity of approximately 9 million+ sqm of Glazed Vitrified Tiles.
evidence.quote: To cater to the growing Southern market, the Company has announced a new manufacturing facility with an annual capacity of approximately 9 million+ sqm. of Glazed Vitrified Tiles.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins increased by 3.6% to 11.6% for the quarter due to operational efficiencies and capacity utilization.
evidence.quote: As a result of capacity utilization, our EBITDA margins have gone up on operational efficiencies, both on capacity utilization in our plants and also on the JV performances. So EBITDA margins go up by 3.6% to 11.6% for the quarter.

evidence.fact: Natural gas price increases have been between 16% and 18%, and the company passed on all gas price increases.
evidence.quote: Every month, there have been a small increases in gas price. Fortunately, we've been able to pass on all the gas price increase until now. So the current price increase has been between 16% and 18%.

evidence.fact: Blended natural gas price comes in at about INR68 for the North, while South and Morbi are in the mid-70s.
evidence.quote: Yes. So our blended price comes in at about INR68. And South, we're still buying partly in spot. So South is -- South and Morbi are pretty much at the same level, which is close to mid-70s. And in the North, it is slightly lower, which is around the INR68, INR69 level.

evidence.fact: Morbi operations have resumed 100% production.
evidence.quote: Morbi operations have completely started. They have resumed 100% production on very expensive gas

evidence.fact: Overall capacity utilization was largely flat, moving from approximately 80% to 79% for the year.
evidence.quote: Capacity utilization was largely flat from approximately 80% to 79%. So that is largely flat.

evidence.quote: Max plant did -- there's good news there that we almost did a breakeven at Max plant. Corresponding quarter last year, same quarter of Q4, the loss was about INR9 crores.

evidence.fact: Working capital days came down from 17 to 12 days.
evidence.quote: Working capital days also have come down from 17 to 12 days.

evidence.fact: Total capex outlay from now to FY27 end is looked at approximately INR275 crores.
evidence.quote: So from now to '27 end, we have already looked at approximately INR275 crores outlay, which includes the INR220 crores plant plus balancing equipment in various other plants and some more balancing equipment in the Bathware, sanitaryware plant.

evidence.fact: About 65% to 70% of the capex will be funded through internal accruals.
evidence.quote: and we will be funding about 65%, 70% of this through internal accruals.

evidence.quote: The gas price has been extremely volatile. I had mentioned that in the earnings call for the FY26, but the gas price since then has been extremely volatile. Every month, there have been a small increases in gas price.
